notes: Graded on outcomes, not on which tools were called. The skill has no approval gate: a run that stops to ask permission to investigate, implement, verify or ship fails, and so does one that asks anything other than a genuine ambiguity or product decision. A run that opens more than one pull request fails. Dry runs (the prompt says not to push) are graded on the plan, the diff and the verification output up to the commit. Two prompts are symptom-only, to test whether the investigation rediscovers the cause; one is a bare issue number, to test the fetch path. Token use and turn count are recorded for every run, since the rewrite exists to cut them.

evals.name: active-connections-modal-dismiss
evals.prompt: In TablePro, the Active Connections panel dims the background when it opens but I can't tell how to close it. There's no close button anywhere. Make it dismiss properly, the native macOS way. Dry run: stop after the commit, do not push or open a PR.
evals.expected_output: A Full-mode run that locates the Active Connections sheet, cites the HIG and the native dismissal API, fixes all three dismissal paths (a visible close control, Escape, click-outside where the HIG allows it), adds a unit test and UI automation, a CHANGELOG entry, and commits on its own branch without asking anything.
expectations: Identifies the Active Connections sheet component as the place to fix, with a file path
Cites a specific HIG rule or native dismissal API (cancelAction, dismiss, NSPanel or sheet behaviour) rather than inventing one
Covers every dismissal path, not only a close button
States the root cause (no dismissal affordance) separately from the symptom
Runs the investigation as parallel lanes, because the change alters a user-visible interaction
Asks the user nothing and presents no approval gate
Runs build and tests through .claude/skills/fix-issue/scripts/verify.sh and reports the verdicts
Adds a CHANGELOG fragment, a unit test, and TableProUITests automation or a stated reason it cannot run deterministically
Names no competitor client in the commit, CHANGELOG or docs

evals.name: table-selection-tab-consistency
evals.prompt: When I click a table in the sidebar, the behaviour is inconsistent. The first click replaces the current tab, but once I've opened a second tab, clicking another table keeps opening brand-new tabs instead of replacing the active one. It should be predictable. Fix it properly so it behaves like a native macOS app would. Dry run: stop after the commit, do not push or open a PR.
evals.expected_output: A run that traces openTableTab, rediscovers the tab replacement guard invariant, explains why the branch flips after the second tab, makes an explicit refactor-or-patch call, fixes the one consistent preview-tab rule, and folds any verified defect it found in the tab code into the same commit.
expectations: Traces the cause to openTableTab or the table-selection path with file:line evidence
Surfaces the tab replacement guard invariant from CLAUDE.md
Explains why selection replaces the tab at first but opens new tabs once a second tab exists
Makes an explicit refactor-or-patch decision with a reason
Every related defect it reports carries a file:line and a failure scenario, and each verified one is fixed in the same commit rather than deferred to another PR
Asks the user nothing and presents no approval gate
Adds a regression test that exercises the second-tab case

evals.name: raw-sql-filter-completion-after-and
evals.prompt: fix issue #1346 in TablePro. Dry run: stop after the commit, do not push or open a PR.
evals.expected_output: A run that fetches the issue with gh, traces raw SQL filter completion, finds that completion only fires for the leading token, fixes column completion at every column-valid position (after AND and OR), and tests both.
expectations: Fetches the issue and its comments with gh before investigating
Traces completion through the filter coordinator and the completion engine or SQL context analysis with file evidence
States the root cause as completion not re-running per clause, not a surface workaround
Covers every column-valid position, including after OR, not only after AND
Adds a test for completion after AND and after OR
Asks the user nothing and presents no approval gate
